bull.b: FedEx Express is the core earnings engine, combining strong revenue growth with four-year-high margins. Sustained yield improvement and international share gains could support durable profitability if network utilization remains healthy.

Network 2.0 and related transformation initiatives provide a multi-year path to lower unit costs and better asset utilization. Progress through optimized stations could make margin gains more durable across the parcel network.

bull.t: Improved Cash Generation and Balance Sheet
bull.b: Stronger free cash flow and sharply lower leverage improve financial flexibility for investment, debt management and shareholder returns. The healthier balance sheet also reduces exposure to prolonged freight, labor or demand weakness.

bear.b: Labor, purchased-transportation and inflationary costs create a persistent risk that revenue and yield gains will not fully convert into operating profit. Contractual wage and pilot costs can remain embedded in the cost base.

The Freight spin simplifies the portfolio but removes a contributor that was already underperforming and leaves transitional stranded costs. Management expects mitigation by end-2027, so earnings may face a multi-period drag before benefits appear.

Revenue growth increasingly depends on pricing, fuel surcharges and favorable mix rather than broad-based volume expansion. Persistent declines in lower-yield or domestic shipments could weaken network density and limit operating leverage.
